four hundred.

post.description:
The logout token is verified against the realm keys before anything is revoked. The call
carries no session cookie and no bearer, because the provider makes it server to server:
the signed token is the whole authentication, which is why this route stands outside the
CSRF guard beside the forge webhook (AP-29).

post.description:
It answers with JSON rather than a 302 on purpose: the SPA calls this with `fetch`, and a
cross-origin redirect to Keycloak is unreadable to it. The browser navigation is the caller's.

`GET /api/v1/auth/sso-check` — asks the realm, without showing anything, whether the person's

get.description:
The Open page loads it in a hidden frame of its own origin when a framed App stays silent, and
reads the answer off the frame's address once it lands on [`SSO_CHECK_DONE`]: only a realm that
says the person must sign in brings the sign-in offer, never the App's silence alone.

answer is in its fragment, which the browser never sends, so the page carries nothing and runs
nothing: the Open page reads the frame's address itself.

post.summary: JSON-RPC 2.0 dispatcher for the Configuration MCP server.
post.description:
One operation in the document, with an opaque body, because that is what the route is
(T-2402): a single POST whose meaning is the JSON-RPC `method` inside it, not the path. The
alternative — leaving it out because it is not REST — made the API page and the published
contract disagree, and a route a person can call belongs in the contract whatever shape its
body has. The methods themselves are listed on the page (API/01 §21), where a JSON-RPC
surface can be written down properly.

requestBody.description: A JSON-RPC 2.0 request object: `jsonrpc`, `method`, `params`, `id`. The method decides what happens; the path never does (AG-60, ADR-N-021).

200.description: The JSON-RPC response object. A refusal the protocol owns — an unknown method, a bad parameter — is an `error` member here and not an HTTP status

`no-credential`, or `None` when it has one (PF-37, T-5626).

AccountGrant.description:
One entry of a ServiceAccount's `spec.roles` as its Access tab reads it (AG-130): the role and
scope, the window and where it stands, and the Portal rules its `Role` carries, without
`approve`, which no account holds (PF-58). A role that names no `Role` (a gateway template,
CC-60) carries no Portal rule and acts at the gateway alone.

index.description: The position in `spec.roles`, which a revoke names with the role (AG-132).

AccountRule.description:
One rule of the `Role` behind an [`AccountGrant`]: the jc-core [`Rule`] with `approve` taken
out, typed for the OpenAPI document so the Access tab reads `kinds` and `verbs` (AG-130).

constraints.description: Constraints every covered manifest must satisfy, as the Role writes them.

kinds.description: Manifest kinds the rule covers, e.g. `Pipeline`.

verbs.description: Verbs granted on those kinds, e.g. `propose`; never `approve`.

AccountSeen.description: One ServiceAccount of the broker's roles and its connected clients.

since.description: The newest `connected_at` of its connected clients; `null` when none is connected.

alertProjects.description:
The projects in which this caller may subscribe to an agent's alerts (`PUT /alerts`,
scope `agent`): those they approve in, sorted (T-5301).

people.description: The starters of the runs, sorted.

spaces.description: The Context Spaces the runs read, sorted.

details.description:
A small object of named values, never a payload (OPS-48). `details.object` is the
`{plural}/{name}` an object page filters on.

costUsd.description: The sum of the costs the provider reported, in USD; none when no call reported one.

mayStop.description: Whether this caller may stop it now (`POST …/agent-runs/{id}/cancel`).

reason.description: The refusal's problem text, or the reason a write gave; masked.

target.description: What the call named: an Endpoint, a resource, a page; never its arguments.

write.description: The call changes something (its operation is not read-only).

AddDevice.description: A device to add: its account name, the role and topic picked, and its public keys.

jwks.description: A JSON Web Key Set of public keys only (PF-47).

name.description: The ServiceAccount's name, a DNS label such as `sensor-001`.

topic.description: One of the role's publish filters; required when the role publishes.

Affordance.description:
Something the caller may or may not do that no rule expresses as a kind and a verb, with the
API's own words for the refusal: the control is rendered disabled with the reason, never
hidden (UI-44).

reason.description: Why not; absent when the caller may.

alerts.description: The signals over the runs the filters select, newest first; one per agent or run.

choices.description: The values the person and space filters offer: those of the runs this caller sees.

AgentActsAs.description: Whose rights an agent uses (AG-94, AG-115).

count.description: Refusals in the hour, percent of the cap, or writes outside office hours.

runTitle.description: The run's title as its card shows it, so an alert names the run a person recognises.

profile.description: The agent profile a run executes, for `AgentRun` only.

project.description: The namespace: a project, or `org` for the organization's own manifests.

AgentRegistry.description: Every agent the caller may read.

changeId.description:
The `chg-…` id of the Change that publishes the application, read from `merge_request`
when the API answers (AP-71).

endpoints.description:
Every endpoint the run reads, `[{name, slug, space}]`, the primary (`endpoint_name`)
first; `[]` for a run of one endpoint recorded before several were possible (AP-44).

firstFrameMs.description: Milliseconds from creation to the first preview, set once (AP-57).

firstVersionMs.description: Milliseconds from creation to the first generated version, set once.

mirrorUrl.description:
The GitHub copy of the application's repository on the run's branch, when the installation
keeps one (AP-79). The forge's `source_url` stays the repository of record.

origin.description:
`person`, or `journey` for a run the Portal's own live journeys started (AG-93). Only a
browser session sets `journey`; a list leaves those out unless it is asked for them.

sourceUrl.description: The forge's public web address of the run's source, its `path_prefix` on its branch (AP-71).

title.description: The application's name for people, chosen with its first version; `app_name` is the id.

AgentRunStatus.description:
Where one builder run stands (Architecture/19 §5). The wire name of every variant is the
name of the state in that chapter, which is why the rename is `snake_case` and not
`lowercase`: `awaiting_approval` is one state, not one word.

AlertMute.description: How long a subscription stays muted, or `null` to unmute.

AlertNotice.description: One notice left for a subscriber.

pipeline.description: The pipeline, or the agent profile for `refusalSpike`, `spendShare` and `offHoursWrite`.

subscription.description: The subscription it came from, which "Mute" names.

AlertSubscription.description: One subscription as the API shows it.

mutedUntil.description: RFC 3339; none when it is not muted.

Allowance.description: The project's MQTT allowance and its usage (API/01 §47).

raise.description: The sentence a refusal ends with: who can raise the allowance, and where (PF-101).

AnswerRequest.description: An answer to one question the agent asked (AG-45).

AppAudience.description:
How many people each visibility of one App reaches (AP-173). Counted from the bindings in
force and the members of the `Group` manifests they name; a group the identity provider owns
lists no members here, so a count is at least that many people.

publicAllowed.description: Whether the organization allows public Apps (PF-103).

roles.description: Holders of each role the App declares, in the order `spec.roles` lists them.

AppBuild.description: Where an application's build is, and whether this person may ask for another (AP-103).

configurationUrl.description:
The project's configuration repository, the one its Changes merge into; `null` for a
caller the forge does not let read it (AP-103, PF-87, T-3039).

packageUrl.description: The package of `status.build.commit`, `null` while the App has no build.

repositoryUrl.description:
The App's own repository (its whole source, T-3039); `null` for an App not built on the
forge.

oneOf.description: The newest workflow run, `null` before the first.

typicalSeconds.description:
How long the newest finished successful run took, in seconds: the estimate a running
build is shown against (T-3245); `null` before the first one.

AppBuilds.description: The successful builds, newest first, and whether Restore is offered (AP-171).

dataNote.description: What Restore does not roll back.

AppCheck.description: The last probe of one App (AP-136).

AppDashboard.description: The App's dashboard file and what the editor offers for it.

attributes.description: The attributes of that type the person may read: every attribute dropdown offers these.

config.description: The file as the default branch holds it; `null` when the App keeps none.

entityType.description: The entity type the dashboard lists, from its grid.

path.description: The file's path in the App's repository: `src/dashboard.json`.

AppMe.description:
The caller as a published App sees them: the object the static host writes into
`#jc-config` as `user` (AP-95).

roles.description:
The App's roles this person holds, in the order `spec.roles` declares them; empty when
none (AP-92).

AppRole.description: An application role the person holds (PF-94).

modelAvailable.description:
Whether "Generate" can answer now: an agent runner is configured and the model key was
not last reported refused or out of credit (AG-96). When it is `false`, a template is
still used as is (T-5617).

ApproveBody.description: Request body for approving or rejecting a change proposal.

reason.description: Why a change is rejected; written on the merge request beside who rejected it.

ApproveRequest.description: The approver's second look: the subject typed again, never kept.

subject.description: The value of the class's `dataSubjectRef` slot, as the proposal named it.

Artifacts.description:
What one Model Tools run rendered. Every artifact is optional: a version that does not
render one omits it, and a source that does not compile yet answers with `errors` filled in
and the artifacts absent. A half-written model is the normal state of an editor.

brokerSchema.description:
The model with its imports merged, in the LinkML subset the broker reads: what the
reconciler writes to a Context Space's broker tenant (`PUT /q/schemas/{tenant}`, T-3703).

docs.description:
The documentation page, one Markdown file for the whole model: the same page
`jcctl model generate` commits beside the source, so the editor previews what a
reviewer will approve rather than a second rendering of it (DM-02, DM-32, DM-43).

errors.description: Compilation messages. Non-empty with no artifacts means the source does not compile.

generatorVersion.description:
The generator version that produced these artifacts, so a preview and a committed
artifact set can be compared (DM-19).

linkml.description:
The LinkML source itself, which an import produces and the editor then edits; its
annotations carry `spec.source.repository`, `path` and `commit` (DM-07, DM-08).

qb.description:
`model.qb.ttl`, the RDF Data Cube structure, only for a model that declares a Data
Structure Definition (DM-60).

typescript.description: `jc-types.ts`: the row types a generated application compiles against (SDK-10).

costUsd.description: What the provider billed, in USD; absent when the assistant did not answer.

Attribute.description:
One attribute of a class as the space's model states it (T-3223): what an editor needs to map
a field onto it.

description.description: What it means, in the model's words.

maximum.description: The largest value a number may have.

minimum.description: The smallest value a number may have.

oneOf.description: The entity type a relationship points at, and whether it holds several.

required.description: Whether every entity of the class must carry it.

oneOf.description: The unit a quantity is in.

valueType.description:
The JSON type of its value (`string`, `number`, `integer`, `boolean`, `object`, `array`),
absent when the model leaves it open.

values.description: The values a coded attribute may take.

AttributeBinding.description:
One mapped attribute: `from` the record field (two for a point), absent for an expression or
a fixed value.

AttributeExplained.description: What decided one attribute for the caller.

decision.description: The gateway's decision; `None` when it was not asked (the caller may read no Policy).

policy.description: The deciding Policy's manifest name, only for a caller who may read it.

policyHidden.description: A Policy decided and the caller may not read it.

reason.description: `policy_grant_matched`, `prohibited`, `no_grant` or `not_admitted`, as the gateway says.

AttributeOption.description: One attribute and what can draw it.

AttributeQuality.description:
One attribute of one type: how many entities carry it and, for numbers, their range and the
values far outside the rest.

outlierExamples.description: At most five ids of entities holding such a value.

outliers.description: Values outside the Tukey fences (1.5 interquartile ranges past the quartiles).

present.description: Entities of the type that carry the attribute.

AwaitedChange.description: A change another one waits on (MF-48).

BackChannelLogoutForm.description: The provider's back-channel logout call: one signed token, no session and no bearer (AP-29).

logout_token.description: The JWT the provider signed, carrying the `logout_events` claim.

Binding.description: One topic filter's way to an attribute; it ends at the first hop the caller may not read.

attributes.description: The output mapper's map; absent for a step written by hand.

Branding.description: Everything the Portal shows that names or themes an installation.

appsOrigin.description:
The origin published Apps are served from (`JC_PORTAL_APPS_URL`), absent when they are
served on the Portal's own. Never taken from the branding file: the route overwrites it
from the Portal's configuration on every answer, and the in-Portal page of an App frames
it there (AP-122, T-2840).

city.description: The city or region this installation serves.

oneOf.description: The colour tokens the UI writes as CSS custom properties.

contactEmail.description: The DCAT-AP contact point and the footer's address.

documentationBaseUrl.description:
Where this installation serves the User Guide, or empty when it serves none (UI-02,
DP-11). A create form joins it with the page its kind's arrangement names and offers one
link; an installation that leaves it empty shows no link at all, because a dead link is
worse than none. Nothing follows it: it becomes an `href` a person may click and never a
request the Portal makes.

favicon.description: Favicon file, served from the platform's own origin.

oneOf.description: The font stacks the UI writes as CSS custom properties.

hiddenSections.description:
The project sections this installation hides (`dashboards` while `JC_PORTAL_DASHBOARDS`
is not `true`, T-2874). Like `apps_origin`, set by the route from the configuration, so
what a branding file says is overwritten; always sent, so the UI never mistakes a shown
section for one it has not heard about.

instanceName.description: Full name: page titles and the login page.

oneOf.description: The locales the language switcher offers.

logo.description: Logo file, served from the platform's own origin.

orgDomain.description: The organization's domain: URN segment, realm display name, `did:web`.

organisation.description: The legal publisher, which is also the DCAT-AP `dcterms:publisher`.

primaryDark.description:
The primary colour as a dark page paints it: the brand lightened towards white, because
a navy button on a navy page is not a button. Computed, never authored.

primaryForeground.description:
Readable text on top of the primary colour. Always computed from that colour, never
taken from the file: the block names a primary colour but no foreground, and white on
a light primary is unreadable (WCAG 1.4.3). A value in the file is overwritten.

primaryForegroundDark.description:
Readable text on top of `primary_dark` — on the lightened colour, not on the configured
one. The dark theme used to rule that this is always the branded text pushed to black,
which left a `#111827` installation at 2.31:1 and a `#0000bf` one at 3.43:1 (T-2324,
UI-30). Computed here because the choice needs the ratio of the lightened colour.

shortName.description:
Short name: sidebars, tabs, e-mail subjects. A block that omits it gets the full name,
so the field default is empty rather than the struct's.

oneOf.description:
Proposal validation strictness (PF-57). In strict mode, proposals require a fresh
green verdict; in lax mode, Green-lane proposals proceed with a warning.

Broker.description: One broker as the Portal sees it.

declared.description: `false` for the implicit `main` of an organization that declares no broker.

entities.description: The load: the entities its spaces hold, as API/01 §29 counts them.

reason.description: Why the broker is `down` or `unknown`, or why a space's count is missing.

spaces.description: The spaces living on it, as `project/space`.

Build.description: One deploy artifact: the commit it was built from and the OpenAPI document it speaks (T-2485).

commit.description: Empty when the build named none (a local `cargo run` or `pnpm build`).

openapi.description: The sha256 of the OpenAPI document, hex; empty when unknown.

BuildEntry.description: One successful build of an App, as Restore offers it (AP-171).

endpoints.description: An endpoint not named here is `read`.

segment.description:
The connector segment the conversation runs as (T-5958, API/14 §1), e.g. `pipeline`: the
assistant calls that segment's registry tools natively, checked as a connector's calls.

truncated.description: More messages are kept than `limit` answered.

window.description: The capture's window, an ISO 8601 duration; absent outside `capture`.

clientId.description: The device, where a publish filter of the broker names it as `${clientid}`.

payload.description: UTF-8 text when the payload decodes, else base64.

Catalogue.description: The catalogue index: the mirror's, or the one Model Tools caches and refreshes daily (DM-12).

failed.description: The models the mirror could not convert, each with its finding.

refreshedAt.description: When the cache was last filled from the catalogue.

stale.description:
The last refresh did not reach the catalogue, so this index is the older cached one.
An index a browser cannot refresh is still an index it can work from (DM-12).

CatalogueCalendar.description: One calendar output of an Endpoint: its name, its title per language and its `.ics` address.

title.description: The title per language (`sk`, `en`); empty: the name stands for it.

CatalogueClass.description: One class of the model, described as its LinkML describes it.

CatalogueContact.description: Where questions about the dataset go: a role address (EP-80).

CatalogueDataModel.description: The data model behind a dataset.

docsUrl.description: The model's documentation, the dataset's Markdown schema resource.

CatalogueDataset.description: A dataset as the list shows it.

themes.description: EU data-theme codes (`ECON`, `ENVI`, …); the UI names them in the reader's language.

CatalogueDatasetDetail.description: One dataset, as its page shows it.

catalogueUrl.description: The dataset on the catalogue's own site.

oneOf.description: The Endpoint of this installation the dataset describes, when it names one.

frequency.description: The EU frequency the record names (`dct:accrualPeriodicity`).

oneOf.description: The model the Endpoint's space holds.
The dataset's quality score in its public form: counts and dates, no names (T-5112).

CatalogueDraft.description: The two blocks the flow proposes, and what nothing could fill.

attributes.description: The model's attributes per type, and whether the public dataset can carry each one.

catalog.description: The drafted `spec.catalog` (EP-78), or the one the Endpoint already declares.

makesPublic.description: The Endpoint's audience is not `public`: the proposal makes it public, in the red lane.

publish.description: The drafted `spec.publish` (EP-62), or the one the Endpoint already declares.

CatalogueDraftRequest.description: Which Endpoint of the project to draft for.

CatalogueEndpoint.description: The Endpoint a dataset describes, on this installation's own host.

calendars.description: Its calendar outputs, in the order the Endpoint lists them (API/11 EP-159).

feeds.description: Its feed outputs, in the order the Endpoint lists them (EP-150, EP-151).

representations.description: The representations it serves, which decide the "Use this data" snippets.

CatalogueEntry.description: One Smart Data Models catalogue entry as the pickers list it (DM-12, DM-63).

keyword.description: The keywords datasets carry, offered when a dataset is published (T-4948); no filter.

CatalogueFailure.description: A catalogue model the mirror could not convert, listed instead of offered half broken.

finding.description: Why it did not convert, in the converter's words.

CatalogueFeature.description: One located entity: its id, its geometry and its key attributes as text.

CatalogueFeed.description: One feed output of an Endpoint: its name, its title per language and its three documents.

title.description: The title per language (`sk`, `en`); empty: the name stands for it.

CatalogueFeedLink.description: One document of a feed output.

CatalogueLicence.description: A licence as the catalogue's register names it.

CatalogueMap.description:
The located entities of a dataset, read through its Endpoint for the dataset page's map
(EP-82, T-5628).

basemap.description: The project whose basemap draws under the features, when the platform has a basemap.

features.description: One per entity with a GeoJSON geometry, at most 1000.

fields.description: The key attributes a popup and the list show, in display order, labelled in `lang`.

total.description: Entities of the type the Endpoint holds, located or not, when it counted them.

CatalogueMapField.description: One attribute a popup shows (DM-99, DM-100).

CatalogueModel.description: One model of the Smart Data Models catalogue index, as the wizard lists and searches it.

attributes.description: Attribute names, so the wizard can search by attribute without fetching the model.

commit.description: The upstream commit the model was converted from (DM-08), where the mirror answers.

facets.description: Counts per facet value, each over the datasets every other filter keeps.

total.description: Datasets matching the search and every filter.

unavailable.description: Catalogues that did not answer; the others still did.

CataloguePublisher.description: The CKAN organization a dataset belongs to: one per project (Architecture/21 §1).

CatalogueSample.description: Up to ten entities of a dataset, read through its Endpoint (EP-82).

CatalogueSubject.description: One subject of the catalogue: `dataModel.Environment` and the models under it.

CatalogueTemporal.description: The period a dataset covers; either end may be open.

CatalogueTheme.description: An EU data theme: its code and its English name (the UI names it in the reader's language).

Ceiling.description: A ceiling each broker is held to on its own.

kinds.description: The verbs a connector may tick per kind of the presets; a verb left out is greyed.

maxDays.description: The longest life a connector may get, in days.

segments.description: The presets a connector of the caller may carry, e.g. `["data-read"]`.

writes.description: Whether a connector of the caller may hold a write item.

Change.description: The `Change` resource describing a proposed configuration update.

ChangeAuthor.description: Human author attributed on the change proposal.

ChangeDecision.description: Who decided a closed change: the approver of a merge, the rejecter of a closed one.

at.description: RFC 3339, when the forge merged or closed it.

reason.description: The rejecter's reason, when they gave one.

via.description: The connector an autonomous approval came through (T-6552), e.g. `doprava-in-claude`.

ChangeFile.description:
One file of the merge request behind a change (T-0861, MF-21, CC-63).

A bundle merge request carries more than its headline: the approval walks every file and
the strictest lane among them decides the confirmation (T-0832), so the page has to show
the same list. What the approver reads is what the server checks.

fields.description:
This manifest's own field-level diff, base against head and redacted (T-1397); absent for
a native file, which carries no manifest to diff.

kind.description: The manifest's kind, or the kind the directory names for a native file beside one.

lane.description: The lane this file alone would take.

operation.description: What the merge request does to it, from the forge's own diff status.

next.description: The `page` that continues a history listing, while the forge has older ones.

outside.description:
The open merge requests of the project repository that are not Changes, a fork's or a
non-writer's, and why; listed to an organization administrator alone (T-3433).

name.description:
Identifier formatted as `chg-` plus eight lowercase hex characters derived
from the merge request.

ChangeProposal.description: A change proposal representing an open Git merge request.

ci.description:
The repository's CI on the head commit (CC-90): `success`, `pending`, `failure` or
`error`; on the detail of one change, and absent while no check has reported.

oneOf.description:
Who merged or rejected a closed change, when and why, as the Portal recorded it on the
forge (T-3292); absent on an open change and on one closed in the forge itself.

fileCount.description: How many files the merge request changes, the headline manifest included.

files.description:
Every file the merge request changes, on the detail of one change (T-0861). Absent in
a listing, which carries `fileCount` instead: the list would otherwise read every
file of every open change to render a number.

waitsOn.description:
The changes this one waits on, each with where it stands (MF-48): it names what they
create, so it merges after them, and a `Rejected` one flags it.

workspace.description:
The workspace this Change brings back, so the approver reads that it was worked on as a
copy first, and whose (UI-63, CC-79).

ChangeStatus.description: Approval and reconciliation status of a change.

oneOf.description:
The channel the Change was proposed through when it was not the person at the Portal
(AG-137, ADR-N-060 §2.2): read back from the merge request's `Proposed-Via` line.

repository.description:
The one repository the Change targets (CC-87): the organization's, or in layout 2 a
project's own.

ChangeSummary.description: Human-readable proposal summary parameters derived from the plan diff.

ChatRequest.description: A question to an assistant (API/05 §1.1); `jc-assistant` holds every bound.

connectors.description: The connectors switched on; none sent leaves every one on.

conversation.description: The id the first answer gave, to continue its conversation.

ChatTurn.description: One turn of what the person's chat holds (API/05 §1.1).

CkanStatus.description: The CKAN picture of one project.

instances.description: Every catalogue this project can publish to.

publications.description: One entry per endpoint that declares `spec.publish.ckan`.

ClassAttributes.description: A class of the space's model and its attributes (T-3223).

attributes.description:
Required attributes first, then by name; `id` and `type` are the entity's own and not
listed.

description.description: What the class means, in the model's words.

model.description: The model's manifest name and the version the space pins.

type.description: The class, which is the entity type.

isBoundary.description:
Whether naming it binds the connector (a published client id) or only says whom it is
meant for (a loopback client anyone can name, AG-153).

refused.description:
Why the caller's ceiling refuses it, e.g. `DelegationPolicy p does not allow the client
mcp-hub`; absent when it may be named. Create checks it again (T-6309).

when.description: An NGSI-LD `q` evaluated in the page on the rows it shows.

Colours.description:
The five colours a page is built from. Each is validated as a hex triplet or sextet before
it is served, because the UI writes it into a CSS custom property and a value that is not a
colour is a way into the page (OPS-46).

secondary.description: Secondary accent used for links and focus.

author.description: Who wrote it: their username, as the Portal knows them.

authorName.description: What the Portal shows for the author.

mentions.description: The people the comment notified, by identifier.

mine.description: The caller wrote it, so they may remove it.

CommentView.description: One comment as the caller reads it.

unknownMentions.description: Mentions of people who may not read the space: kept in the text, notified to nobody.

Commented.description: A new comment, with the mentions that notified nobody.

Comparison.description: What a workspace changes against its base, and where main changed the same files (API/01 §22).

reason.description: Machine-readable reason code.

Confirmation.description: One broker question as its page shows it to the person who asked.

oneOf.description: `None` until the person decided.

expiresAt.description: Unix seconds after which the broker no longer takes a decision.

message.description: The words the client was handed, shown again on the page.

tool.description: The MCP tool that would run, `create_entity`.

view.description: The broker view the write goes through, `bb-air`.

ConflictPolicy.description: What to do with a resource the project already has (MF-23).

ConnectorApproval.description: Who let a request above the ceiling through, and when.

ConnectorCall.description: One row of a connector's audit (AG-147).

subject.description: The Keycloak subject of the token, the owner's unless the call was refused for it.

target.description: `project/kind/name`, as far as the call names them.

tool.description: The tool, or the MCP method of a call that names none.

ConnectorGrant.description: A connector as its owner reads it (API/14 §1).

aboveCeiling.description:
What the request asked above the owner's DelegationPolicy ceiling; set while pending and
kept after an approval.

autonomous.description: Whether the changes it applies are approved at once as its owner (T-6552).

clientIsBoundary.description:
Whether the allowed clients bind the connector (claude.ai, ChatGPT) or only say whom it
is meant for (Claude Code, `mcp-local`): AG-153.

kinds.description: Verbs per kind (T-6302); absent: every change the segments reach.

limits.description: What the connector may spend; shown on My connectors.

narrowedBy.description:
The parts of this connector the owner's DelegationPolicy ceiling takes away today, each
one line such as `segment pipeline`; calls run without them (AG-150, "narrowed by
policy"). Empty when it fits.

state.description:
`active`, `pending` (above the ceiling, waiting for an administrator), `expired` or
`revoked`.

url.description: The MCP address a client adds: `https://portal.{domain}/c/{id}`.

kind.description: A kind the segments reach, e.g. `Endpoint`.

ConnectorLimits.description:
What one connector may spend (T-5968): calls at once and answer size; calls a minute have no
limit (owner 2026-11-02, T-6484). The person's own budget (`PERSON_LIMITS`) holds across all
their connectors and `/api/v1/mcp` together, so a second connector adds no parallel calls.
Counted on the verified token's subject and the connector id from the path, never on a header.

parallelCalls.description: Calls answered at once; the next answers 429 until one ends.

resultBytes.description:
The largest tool answer in bytes; a larger one is refused as a 413 tool error naming
what to narrow.

ConnectorOptions.description:
What the caller may put in a connector today: the ceiling, and per project they read the
spaces, Endpoints and pipelines they read there (the "My connectors" tree, T-5951).

clients.description: The realm's MCP clients a connector may be bound to, e.g. `mcp-local` (Claude Code).

segmentKinds.description:
The kinds each preset that plans changes reaches, one row each in the dialog's verb table
(T-6302); `data-read` proposes nothing and has none.

segments.description: Every preset a connector may name; those outside `ceiling.segments` need approval.

denialsFlag.description: Refused calls in a day that flag a connector.

ConnectorPatch.description: The fields of a connector its owner may change (JSON merge patch, API/14 §2); the name stays.

autonomous.description: Approve each applied change at once as the owner (T-6552), e.g. `true`.

kinds.description: Verbs per kind, replacing the whole list (T-6302).

ConnectorScopeItem.description:
One item of a connector's scope: a project, and at most one of a space, an Endpoint or a
pipeline in it (`*` for every one the owner reaches). Without one it is the whole project.

personalData.description:
Whether answers through this item keep the attributes the model marks `personalData`
(DM-122): off by default, and only where the organization's ceiling allows it (AG-158).

callsPerDay.description: Calls in the last 24 hours, allowed and refused.

denialsPerDay.description: Refused calls in the last 24 hours.

flagged.description: [`DENIALS_FLAG`] refused calls or more in the last 24 hours.

ConnectorUsage.description:
A connector as an organization administrator reads it (T-5975): its grant and how much it is
used, never what a call carried.

Consent.description:
One client a person consented to (the hub, an Endpoint's MCP client, an App), as the realm's
admin API lists it (T-3792). Never a token: Keycloak keeps those to itself.

Consequence.description: One thing that leaves with a removed resource (T-3247).

names.description: The resources it names, as `Kind/name`, when they are resources.

CostPrices.description: The operator's price table: what the cloud bills a month.

fixed.description: Billed every month whatever runs: addresses, backups.

perUsd.description: The table's currency for one US dollar, which the model provider bills in.

measuredAt.description: When the bytes were measured: storage is read now, not averaged over the month.

Costs.description: A month of the installation split per project, in the price table's currency.

Counts.description: The checks of one rule in one window.

passRate.description: `pass` over all four; `null` when nothing was checked in the window.

project.description:
The project the invitation leads into: its home page greets the person once their
password is set (PF-108). It grants nothing.

CreateRunRequest.description: What a person asks for when they start a run (AP-51).

appClass.description:
`ui`, `ui-rust` or `wasm`, as the `App` kind spells them (AP-124, T-3575); `static` and `fullstack` are
read as them for one release, and `ui-node` is refused until it is built.

appName.description: Name of the application to build; becomes the `App` manifest's name.

dataNeeds.description:
The types, attributes and operations the application needs. Checked against what the
endpoint publishes before anything is scheduled (AP-44).

endpointName.description:
The one `Endpoint` the application reads through; `endpointNames` for several. Nothing
else is reachable.

endpointNames.description: The `Endpoint`s the application reads, one to five, the first the primary (AP-44).

kind.description: What kind of run to execute: application, dashboard, analysis.

profile.description: Which `AgentProfile` runs. Defaults to the builder profile the platform ships.

prompt.description: What the application should do, in the person's own words.

unattended.description: Whether the run executes unattended without interactive questions.

visibility.description: Who may reach the published application. `public` is refused (AP-42).

manifest.description: A Pipeline manifest; only its `spec` is kept, without what belongs to the project.

title.description: What the gallery shows, 1 to 120 characters.

CreatedPerson.description: The one answer that may carry a temporary password, once (PF-92).

memberOf.description:
The Organization whose `/{organization}/members` group the person joined, so they sign
in as its member with no project (ADR-N-067 §2.5); absent when the realm has no such group.

DashboardEdit.description: The edited file, and whether to only preview it.

dryRun.description: `true` answers the file before and after and writes nothing.

DashboardProposal.description: What an edit proposes: the file before and after, and the Change once it is proposed.

oneOf.description: The Change that proposes the App at the edited commit; absent on a dry run.

pullRequestUrl.description: The App repository's merge request the approval merges; absent on a dry run.

unanswered.description: Cells the gateway did not answer for.

DataView.description: A saved view as the API answers it.

measuredAt.description: The newest measurement among the parts, RFC 3339.

score.description: The mean of the parts that have a score; absent while none has.

oneOf.description: What the publisher changes; absent in the public catalogue and when nothing is wrong.

measuredAt.description: When the part was measured, RFC 3339.

score.description: 0 to 100; absent while nothing measures the part.

DatasetScoreText.description:
A message of the score: its key under `quality.score.say` in the UI's locales with the
values it names, and its English.

Day.description: One Endpoint's calls on one day, by surface.

DeadLink.description: A link that failed [`DEAD_AFTER`] checks in a row.

error.description: Why it did not answer (a timeout, a refused connection).

status.description: The status it answered, none when it did not answer.

Decision.description: Why an owner declines or revokes.

DecisionRequest.description: The person's answer to one question.

decision.description: `accept` lets the call run once; `decline` refuses it.

DeclineRequest.description: Why the proposal is declined, for the audit record.

DeviceOptions.description: What the Add device form of one broker may offer the caller.

issuer.description: The `aud` of the device's client assertion: the realm issuer.

mayAdd.description: Whether the caller may propose a device here: `ServiceAccount` and this `MqttBroker`.

tokenUrl.description: The realm's token endpoint a device asks for its access token, absent without a login.

DeviceRole.description: One role the form may offer, with the topic filters a device of it may publish to.

passed.description:
The keys that passed, for a check whose passes a page shows (`apps`, AP-136); empty for
every other check.

challenge.description: What the TXT record carries after `jc-verify=`. Not a secret: it is published in DNS.

reason.description: Why a `failed` domain failed, in words a person acts on; never a resolver's answer.

record.description: The record to publish, spelled out: `_joinedcontext.{domain} TXT "jc-verify={challenge}"`.

workspace.description:
The workspace the draft belongs to, or none (CC-76): a draft of one workspace is not
a draft of another, nor of the main project.

DraftAttribute.description: One attribute of one type the Endpoint serves, as the publish form lists it.

type.description: The class (entity type) the attribute belongs to.

oneOf.description: Why it is not offered; absent when the public dataset may carry it.

DraftList.description: Collection of drafts returned by the list operation.

DraftProjection.description: The part of a `ModelProjection` the editor changes.

DropDraftResponse.description: Confirmation payload after dropping a draft.

DryRun.description: The answer of the dry run.

clientId.description: The client id and username the device connects with: its Keycloak client.

DryRunResult.description: Reviewer-facing validation and diff result returned on `?dryRun=All` (MF-13, R17).

findings.description:
Values the manifest writes out where the loader renders them (CC-83): each names the
path and what to write instead. Nothing here blocks the proposal; a copy of the
manifest into another organization would carry the literal with it.

goesWith.description:
What leaves with a removed resource, with how many (T-3247): a space's entities, a
pipeline's refused records and runs, an App's endpoint and policies, the bindings a
Group's removal edits. Empty for every write that is not a removal.

oneOf.description: What one fetch of an `http` DataSource returned (MF-39); absent for every other kind.

restartsStream.description:
Whether applying this makes the runner restart the pipeline's stream, so a person sees
it before approving rather than afterwards (T-1056, PL-45). Absent for every other kind.

oneOf.description: The verdict this check recorded for the manifest, which its proposal needs (PF-57, T-0956).

DuplicateProject.description: The new slug of a duplicate and this deployment's own values.

name.description: The copy's slug: the `{project}` segment of every path of it (PF-67).

parameters.description: Values for the parameters the origin's `project.yaml` declares (CC-88).

Edge.description: One directed relation between two nodes.

manifest.description: The manifest this edge was read from, as `kind/name`, so a reader can open it.

EditOffer.description: Whether Edit is offered, and why not when it is not.

Effective.description: What one caller may do in one project: `GET /api/v1/projects/{project}/permissions/me`.

bootstrap.description:
The caller is in the bootstrap group of `JC_PORTAL_BOOTSTRAP_ADMINS`: everything,
everywhere, so the first binding can be written into an empty repository.

oneOf.description:
Filled by the route, not by the rules: opening a project is the organization's own
setting and no binding expresses it (PF-65, T-0870).

ElicitationDecision.description: What the person decided on the Portal page.

EndpointAccess.description: What the assistant may prepare on one endpoint's entities.

EndpointLicence.description: A licence of the EU licence table.

code.description: The EU licence table code, such as `CC_BY_4_0`.

url.description: The licence's IRI in the EU licence table.

EndpointOption.description: One Endpoint the caller may read.

usable.description: Grafana can read it: public, or its slug is in the project's datasources.

EndpointStandards.description: What a public Endpoint's page shows under "Standards".

base.description: The Endpoint's public address, ending in `/`: every sample a developer page shows starts here.

entityType.description: The type of the entity the examples were built from; absent when none was read.

oneOf.description: The licence the Endpoint's catalogue entry names; absent when it names none.

requestsPerMinute.description:
The requests a minute the edge lets one anonymous caller send (ADR-N-035, class
`publicEndpoint`); beyond it the edge answers 429.

served.description: Every representation the Endpoint serves, query standards and files alike.

types.description: The entity types of the Endpoint's data model.

EndpointTotal.description: One Endpoint's line in the project's usage.

callers.description: The window's calls by kind of caller: person, workload, agent, anonymous, unknown (T-6186).

daily.description: Calls per day, oldest first, one number for every day of the window.

EndpointUsage.description: One Endpoint's usage over a window, a row for every day, empty days included.

callers.description:
The window's calls by kind of caller, one of person, workload, agent, anonymous or
unknown (counted before the gateway told them apart; T-6186).

EventReceipt.description: The sequence number a relayed event was given.

Example.description: A query that answered with at least one entity when the page was built.

answered.description: The entities on the first page of its answer.

consents.description: A person's Keycloak consents; empty for every other kind.

mcpServers.description: The project's McpServers with a member among `endpoints`.

FailedRequest.description: A request of the frame the bridge answered with an error status.

Failure.description: One result of the last run that did not pass, and the open task it filed.

edges.description: Directed edges, each naming the manifest it was read from.

nodes.description: Every object the federation touches, keyed by `kind/name`.

Feedback.description: One feedback as the administrators' list shows it.

screenshot.description: Whether a screenshot was sent with it.
A PNG `data:` URL, only when the person ticked it.

FieldChange.description:
A single leaf field modification in a plan diff.

Paths are dotted strings rooted at `metadata` or `spec` (e.g. `spec.audience`,
`spec.representations[1]`, `metadata.labels.joinedcontext.com/domain`).
Keys containing dots (such as reverse-DNS label names) are deliberately not escaped.

FieldConflict.description: One field both sides changed to different values since their common base (CC-80).

FieldError.description:
One violation: the member it is about and what is wrong with it (AG-146). `path` is the
member's dotted path (`spec.history[1]`), or empty when the finding is about the whole request.

FileConflict.description:
One file both the workspace and main changed since the workspace's base (CC-80). `fields`
lists what a person has to choose; empty means the two sides merge on their own, which
updating from main does.

FlowGrant.description: What permits a pipeline to read or write through an Endpoint.

fix.description: What to change when it is missing.

operation.description: The operation the edge needs, as a Policy names it.

policy.description: The Policy that grants it, named only to a caller who may read Policy in its space.

FlowKind.description: What a node is on the map.

FlowMap.description: The map of one project, or of the paths that touch one of its spaces.

FlowNode.description:
One resource on the map. Only facts a reader of the manifest already sees: no secret, no
credential, no URL path or query (a token can ride in one), only a source's host.

hosts.description: The hosts a DataSource connects to, without user, path or query.

opaque.description: Another project's resource the caller may not read: its name, nothing else.

phase.description: A pipeline's phase as the reconciler last set it.

slug.description: An Endpoint's address segment and its audience.

space.description: The space an Endpoint reads and writes.

topics.description: The topic filters an MQTT DataSource subscribes to.

FlowRelation.description: How data moves along an edge.

FlowRequest.description: Running a blueprint: the parameters the form collected (API/01 §13).

parameters.description: The values the user filled in, validated against `spec.parameterSchema` (CC-24).

version.description:
The version the form was generated from. A mismatch is a conflict rather than an
expansion against a schema the user never saw (CC-26).

FlowRole.description:
What a pipeline does on the map: reads the outside world, computes from a space, or writes
indicators (PL-45). A space ending in `-kpi` is an indicator space (PF-54).

FlowRun.description: A pipeline's latest run, as the Portal logged it (PL-62).

at.description: The last line the Portal took for it, RFC 3339.

perMinute.description: Records sent per minute over the run, when it lasted a minute or more.

Fonts.description:
Heading and body font stacks. Self-hosted or system families only: nothing on a page
fetches from a third-party origin at runtime.

FormContextRequest.description: The form the question was asked from, as the browser sends it (API/04 §"Start or Continue").

Freshness.description: How recent the data of one pipeline is.

type.description: The pipeline's output type; empty when it names none and the whole space counts.

Front.description:
How a request authenticated: what `GET /api/v1/auth/me` reports so the UI knows whose
logout to call (ADR-N-019 §3.4).

source.description: LinkML YAML, exactly as the editor holds it.

GrafanaOptions.description: What the form's dropdowns may offer this person now.

items.description: Those whose Endpoint the caller may read, newest first.

mayCreate.description: The caller may save and remove visualizations here.

ready.description: Grafana answers and holds this project's organization.

reason.description: What a person reads when it does not.

Grant.description: One rule in force, with the binding and role it came through, so a refusal can be traced.

organization.description:
Set when the binding is scoped to an Organization other than the installation's and the
grant is read at [`ORG_NAMESPACE`]: the rule is narrowed to that Organization's own
settings, bindings and groups (ADR-N-058 section 2.4), reads only what its constraints
admit and never makes its holder an administrator of the installation.

scope.description:
Where the binding that carries this rule applies: `organization`, `project:{name}` or
`contextSpace:{name}`. A grant read here may have been inherited from the organization,
and the page says so rather than making it look local (PF-60, PF-61).

space.description:
Set when the binding is scoped to one context space: the rule then applies only to a
manifest whose `spec.contextSpaceRef` names it.

GrantState.description: Where one grant of a ServiceAccount stands at `now` (AG-131).

GrantingRule.description:
One rule of a Policy that grants a column: the Policy, the rule's place (1 is the first of
`rules`, 0 the Policy's own assignee) and the types it names.

Health.description: Whether a broker answered its health.

HealthCheck.description: One check of one resource as the Health page shows it.

check.description:
`reconcile`, `runs`, `freshness`, `entities`, `storage`, `validation`, `reachable`, or a
surface an Endpoint serves (`ngsi-ld`, `odata`, `mcp`, ...).

checkedAt.description: When the leader last judged it, RFC 3339.

detail.description: What the check found, credentials masked.

evidenceUrl.description: The Portal page of the resource.

fix.description: The manifest field or the page to change; empty when there is nothing to fix.

history.description: The statuses of the last 7 days, oldest first.

lastOk.description: When the check was last ok, RFC 3339; absent when it never was.

since.description: Since when this status holds, RFC 3339.

HealthCheckList.description: The checks, errors first, then warnings, then ok.

HealthCheckPoint.description: One point of a check's history.

HealthCheckStatus.description: Errors first, then warnings, then what is well.

HealthCheckText.description:
A message of the health log: its key under `health.say` in the UI's locales with the values
it names, and its English text for the API and the logs. A text a component wrote (a broker's
error) has no key: it is shown as it came, credentials masked.

args.description: The values the message names, by placeholder.

code.description: The key under `health.say`; empty for a component's own words.

bound.description: Held through a RoleBinding `mqtt/<broker>/<role>` or `mqtt/*/<role>` in force.

legacy.description: Held through the role's deprecated `serviceAccounts` list.

publish.description: Topic filters the account's devices may publish to.

role.description: The role's name on the broker.

subscribe.description: Topic filters they may subscribe to.

until.description: When the last grant of the role ends; absent while one has no end.

HoldReason.description: Why a run deleted nothing and alerts the pipeline's subscribers.

Hop.description: One hop of a binding: a manifest by name, or `hidden` when the caller may not read it.

space.description: The Context Space an Endpoint writes into.

Identity.description: Who is signed in. Returned by `GET /api/v1/auth/me` and used by every protected route.

email.description:
Only an address the identity provider verified ([`verified_email`]): a binding's `user`
subject matches it, so an address a person typed in unverified grants nothing.

groups.description:
Keycloak group paths from the token's `groups` claim, without the leading `/`. Identity,
not permission: a `RoleBinding` names a group, the Portal checks the binding (PF-50).

roles.description:
Keycloak realm roles from the ID token's `realm_access.roles` (CC-42). Empty when the
token asserts none. Display and enablement only — the resource API and the forge enforce
the same boundaries independently.

second_factor.description:
The person proved a second factor when this session signed in: the token's `amr` names
`otp`, or its `acr` is the realm's step-up level `mfa`. Every decision door asks for it
(T-5567); `GET /api/v1/auth/me` reports it so the UI can offer the step-up.

subject.description: Keycloak `sub`: stable, opaque, the only durable user key.

ImportOptions.description: The options an import wizard sends beside the file (Architecture/06 §6).

manifests.description: The manifests themselves, for a caller that posts JSON rather than a file.

orgDomain.description:
The organisation domain every imported id is rewritten to; this instance's own
organisation when absent (PF-10, PF-43).

spaceMapping.description:
Spaces the bundle names that are not copied: each reference to `from` lands on the
target project's space `to`, ids included (T-1441, MF-26).

targetNamespace.description: The namespace every imported manifest is rewritten into; the project when absent (MF-22).

url.description: A bundle to fetch rather than upload. Refused for now, see [`import`].

ImportReport.description: What one import would do, answered on a dry run and echoed in the merge request body.

lane.description: The lane the whole bundle lands in: the riskiest of everything it carries (CC-63).

nativeFiles.description: Files carried through untouched: `bento.yaml`, LinkML sources, schema artifacts.

needs.description:
What the bundle cannot carry and has to be provided where it lands (CC-84): secret
values, people, hosts, feed credentials. Empty means nothing is to be provided. Never a
secret value, only where one is set.

reassigned.description:
Policies whose `assigner` the import rewrote to `did:web:{orgDomain}`, as `Policy/{name}`
to the DID the bundle carried: the grant is this organisation's now (CC-82, R6).

renamed.description: Resources imported under a new name, `old -> new` (`rename`).

replaced.description: Resources that would replace one the project already has.

skipped.description: Resources left alone because the project already has them (`skip`).

source.description: Where the bundle came from, when it carried a `kind: Bundle` index (MF-20).

verified.description:
Per file, whether what the import wrote equals the checksum the bundle index carries,
with the namespace mapping undone (MF-42). Empty when the bundle carries no checksums:
an unverifiable transfer says so rather than claiming every file is equal.

ImportSdmRequest.description: A model to import from the Smart Data Models catalogue.

model.description:
Catalogue identifier, `dataModel.Environment/AirQualityObserved`. Never a URL: the
allowlist that limits fetching to the Smart Data Models organisation lives in Model
Tools (DM-10), and the Portal refuses anything a caller could steer.

InclusionRequest.description: Include or exclude pages, their subtrees, and documents (API/01 §34).

included.description: `false` excludes: their passages go at once and the choice holds over later crawls.

subtree.description: Whether every page below the named ones, and the documents they link, change too.

InstanceSummary.description: One `CkanInstance`, without anything secret about it.

apiTokenRef.description: The name of the secret holding the API token. Never its value (EP-67).

organizationDefault.description: The organization a dataset lands in when the endpoint names none.

url.description: Base URL of the catalogue.

IssuedSecret.description: A new client secret, in this answer and nowhere else.

clientId.description: The Keycloak client the external system signs in as, `{project}-{name}`.

clientSecret.description: The secret, shown once: the Portal keeps no copy.

JobRun.description: One job's last run, in `status.jobs[]` (AP-154, AP-155): never a body or a credential.

failuresInARow.description: Runs that failed or timed out in a row; three raise a notice to the owners (AP-155).

lastRun.description: When the run was due, RFC 3339 UTC.

message.description: Why a run did not succeed, in words a person acts on.

KeepRequest.description: The copy of one entity about to be deleted.

entity.description: The NGSI-LD entity as the person read it, normalized.

pipeline.description: The draft `joinedcontext.com/v1alpha2` Pipeline with one `kpi` step.

preview.description: Also compute the indicator on the sources' current pages.

oneOf.description: Present when asked for and the draft has no problem.

problems.description: Empty when the draft is a KPI admission takes.

KpiPreview.description: The indicator on the sources' current pages.

problem.description:
Why nothing is computed: a division by zero, an average over nothing, a source that did
not answer (PL-104), no history for a `prev` term (PL-117).

rows.description: The rows each source's page held, at most 100; a read back goes by `parking@P7D`.

values.description: One value per key, one for a join by time.

KpiProblem.description: One field jc-core refuses, and why.

reason.description: The rule it breaks, in words.

KpiSource.description: What the editor knows of one source.

name.description: The source's `name`, the input's name in the formula.

readable.description:
Whether the pipeline's account reads the source's type through the Endpoint now: a
Policy grants it, its history too for a `prev` term, or the Endpoint is public (PL-55,
PL-90, PL-117).

key.description: The entity or area key; absent for a join by time.

Languages.description: The locale the UI starts in and the ones it offers.

default.description: The locale a first-time visitor gets.

offered.description: Every locale the switcher lists; always contains the default.

LimitEntry.description: One entry of the catalog as the settings page shows it (PF-102).

default.description: The catalog's default; `null` is no limit.

max.description: The largest value the organization may set; `null` where nobody sets a ceiling.

min.description: The smallest value the organization may set.

security.description: Whether the operator may only tighten the bound (ADR-N-035 §3.2).

value.description: What the Organization manifest sets; `null` when it sets nothing.

LimitOrigin.description: Where a value in force comes from (PF-101).

LogoutTarget.description: The URL the browser must visit to finish an RP-initiated logout at Keycloak.

endSessionUrl.description:
Absolute URL: Keycloak's `end_session_endpoint`, or the portal itself when no realm is
configured.

MatrixCell.description: What one principal may do on one type for one action.

attributes.description: `"*"` for every attribute, else the attribute names.

constraint.description: The constraints the grant narrows the rows by (`q`, `scopeQ`, `geoQ`, `temporalQ`).

decidedBy.description: The Policy that grants or prohibits this, when one Policy in force covers the type.

effect.description: `permit`, or `prohibit` where a prohibition takes it away.

MatrixEdge.description:
One edge of the graph principal → Policy → Endpoint → type; node ids are
`principal:{kind}:{name}`, `policy:{name}`, `endpoint:{name}` and `type:{name}`.

MatrixVia.description:
How a principal reaches the Endpoint: a Policy that names it, or the project's
ServiceAccount manifest it is.

front.description:
`portal` for the Portal's own cookie session, `edge` for the APISIX `openid-connect`
session, `bearer` for a token a service sent (ADR-N-019).

Me.description: Who is signed in and through which front, so the UI knows whose logout to call.

accounts.description: Every ServiceAccount the broker's roles name, in name order.

measured.description: `false` when the broker did not answer; `reason` says why and no number is given.

messagesPerSecond.description: `messages.publish` of the two newest samples, per second; `null` with fewer than two.

publishers.description: Connected clients of the accounts whose roles may publish.

rates.description:
Messages per second between each two neighbouring samples the broker keeps (its
`history_retention`, five minutes in the chart), oldest first; empty when not measured.

refusedPublishes.description:
Publishes the broker refused since it started (`client.publish.auth.error` of the newest
sample): the gateway's publish check said no, or the client was over its rate.

MessageRequest.description: What a person says to a run that is already going (AG-45).

oneOf.description: On a conversation: the capabilities from this message on (AG-92, T-2718).

endpointNames.description: On a conversation: the endpoints the assistant may query from this message on (AG-75).

oneOf.description: On a conversation: the page the person is on as they send it (T-2763).

scope.description:
On an application run: the `src` of the preview's `jc-select`, `{file}:{line}`; the
editing agent changes that file only for this message (SDK-46).

Meter.description: One summed limit: what the allowance gives, what the brokers use, and what is left.

left.description: Never below `0`; a project over a lowered allowance shows `used` above `limit` (PF-100).

Method.description: Which of the two proofs verified the domain.

unresolved.description:
Addresses and usernames no Keycloak user carries: they stay as they are, and the
reconciler leaves a group naming one as the realm holds it until somebody fixes it.

ModelChange.description: Single detected difference between the published model and the candidate LinkML source.

to.description: A `ContextBroker` of the organization other than the one the space lives on.

Need.description: One thing a copy cannot carry (CC-84, API/01 §10).

link.description: The Portal page that sets it.

where.description: The manifest and the path inside it, `Kind/name spec.path`.

why.description: Why it has to be provided, in words.

NewAlertSubscription.description: What a person asks to be told about.

NewConnector.description: What a person asks for when creating a connector (API/14 §1).

allowedClients.description: OAuth client ids the connector answers, e.g. a CIMD URL `https://claude.ai/oauth/mcp-client-metadata`.

kinds.description:
Verbs per kind, e.g. `[{"kind": "Endpoint", "verbs": ["read", "create"]}]`; a kind left
